title: Ending live animal displays at Waterloo Park
subtitle: Uptown improvement grants extended, six new plow trucks, auditor reappointed, sanitary master plan, interim tax levy and committee appointments.
overview: Council voted to end the display of live animals at the Eby Farmstead in Waterloo Park ahead of the park plan update {{vote:m12}}. Staff will re-home the animals and dismantle the enclosures during the 2025 construction season. Council also asked staff to speed up choosing a site for an off-leash dog park in the city core, including a possible temporary location. Staff cited the age of the animals and the dated infrastructure, and said the decision would give the 2025 park plan engagement a clearer focus.

Council extended the Uptown Waterloo Community Improvement Plan grants and parking exemption to December 31, 2025, and directed a review of the program, including the BIA {{vote:m10}}. It approved six new plow trucks {{vote:m11}}, reappointed KPMG LLP as auditor for up to five years {{vote:m4}}, and approved the 2025 interim tax levy {{vote:m9}}.

Council also approved the Sanitary Master Plan Update and road widening for the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive project. It heard a university presentation on urban heat islands. Staff said work on a vacant buildings policy should restart early in the first quarter of 2025. A closed meeting was held earlier in the day, and the minutes report no outcome from it.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to end the live animal display, re-home the animals, dismantle the enclosures in 2025, and expedite choosing a dog park location in the city core.
Council extended the Façade Improvement Grant, Major Activity Grant and Parking Exemption program to December 31, 2025 and directed a program review including the BIA.
Council approved buying six commercial plow trucks from Metro Freightliner Hamilton Inc. and Viking Cives Ltd. for a total of $2,595,466 including unrecoverable HST.
Council awarded RFP 24-03 to KPMG LLP for a total of $347,764.80 and reappointed the firm as auditor for up to five years from 2024 to 2028.

Council approved the plan, directed staff to file the notice of completion and start the 30-day review, and to consider priority project costs in the next Development Charges By-law update and capital budgeting.
Council approved the staff report and authorized execution of documents for property acquisitions for the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive reconstruction project.
Council approved the 2025 Interim Tax Levy and its by-law.
Council approved the recommended appointments to the Waterloo Advisory Committee on Active Transportation, voted separately from other committee appointments.

debate: A delegate supported re-homing the animals but proposed using the vacated enclosure as a temporary off-leash dog park. The delegate cited the lack of dog parks in the city core, high visibility, the existing fencing and low cost.

Staff agreed the core needs a dog park but doubted the enclosure was the right site. They cited the need to remove buildings and electrical infrastructure, regrade uneven ground, protect mature trees, fix erosion and upgrade accessibility and gates. They also raised parking demand and conflicts with the nearby accessible playground, and said temporary uses tend to become permanent.

Councillors said the animals are aging and the infrastructure is dated. Keeping a live display would need significant capital and operating money, and staff compared other municipalities' operating costs. One councillor wanted the funds from ending the program to stay in Waterloo Park.

On the dog park direction, councillors wanted speed, and one supported a temporary site with limited engagement. Staff said they needed time to review options, and may defer another capital project to make room.

On the Uptown grants, a councillor asked about reports that applications are onerous. Staff described a short application that can be approved within days, or about a month where heritage or sign by-laws apply. Staff plan to consult past users and the BIA, and councillors cited low awareness among new businesses and landlord consolidation.
